title: Resolve TTFT and tokens/sec slowdown for long-context models across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Kaur
description: Multiple customers reported abrupt TTFT regressions and a sustained drop in tokens/sec when using models with >16k context windows. The problem appears across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but is most pronounced for long-context specialized models (32k+). Initial triage indicates an interaction between the KV-cache index update path and the kernel selection heuristic: when sequences cross a chunk boundary the system triggers a full attention fallback and performs an expensive KV cache compaction/copy that significantly increases scheduling latency and reduces throughput.
impact_summary: A set of enterprise customers (AcmeAI, FinVault, HealthMap) experienced 2-8x TTFT increases and throughput drops hurting user-facing features (chat streaming, summarization). Incidents have triggered customer escalations and SLA risk for Dedicated customers. Hosted customers observed elevated 95/99 percentile TTFTs for specific model variants under long-context workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy model variant with 32k context (internal longctx-alpha or open-model-32k) on a Dedicated worker or use hosted endpoint with model pinned to long-context variant.
2) Start steady traffic of small messages that progressively extend the prefix until token index crosses the 16k boundary; observe initial TTFT baseline.
3) Continue requests that cause the KV cache to evict/compact (many rolling sessions or long single-session generation).
4) Observe TTFT spike in metrics (Grafana dashboard longctx/ttft) and tokens/sec fall on affected worker pool; check worker logs for 'kv_cache_compact' and 'kernel_fallback' messages.
5) Repeat on Private deployment in a staging VPC to confirm behavior in air-gapped environments.
mitigation_workarounds: Short-term hosted workaround: pin customers to the legacy 16k-compatible model variant (model: open-model-16k) and enable conservative kernel selection via feature flag runtime.kernel_override=conservative.
Dedicated: increase worker pool headroom to avoid preemption during compaction and set max_prefix_length=15000 for affected instances.
Private: provide a config patch (kb link) to disable automatic KV-cache compaction (runtime.kv_compact=false) until fixed; warn about memory usage.
Client-side: reduce rolling-session length or send periodic checkpointing requests to avoid large sequential buildup during peak traffic.
proposed_fix: Implement an O(n) in-place KV-cache compaction path and ensure kernel selector checks both sequence-length delta and predicted memory pressure before triggering full-attention fallback. Patch will include:
proposed_fix_details: A) Add unit tests for boundary crossing at powers-of-two chunk sizes and synthetic workloads that force compaction.
B) Implement in-place KV compaction algorithm (patch: GH PR #redwood/runtime#2541) that avoids large buffer copies for common case (small evictions).
C) Update kernel heuristic to consult worker-level memory headroom and per-request expected new_kv_size before switching to fallback kernels.
D) Add a runtime throttle so compaction runs on a background stripe when token throughput is > 1000 tokens/sec to avoid blocking generation threads.
E) Backport hotfix to runtime-1.19-stable branch and prepare rolling deploy playbook for Hosted and Dedicated pools; provide config bundle for Private customers.
qa_checks: Regression tests: end-to-end generation with 8k/16k/32k contexts under burst and steady loads.
Perf tests: compare TTFT and tokens/sec before/after patch on small/medium/large models and on both A100 and T4-like instances.
Canary: deploy to 5% of hosted longctx pool and 2 dedicated customers; monitor 50/95/99p TTFT and tokens/sec for 24h.
Compatibility: ensure no change to model outputs other than timing (snapshot and hash top-k output checks for determinism where applicable).
rollout_plan: Day 0 (hotfix PR): land GH PR #redwood/runtime#2541 to main with feature flag runtime.kv_compact_inplace=true (feature gated).
Day 1: merge and build canary images; deploy to internal staging and run test harness with synthetic long-context traffic.
Day 2: deploy to 5% hosted longctx pool + 2 dedicated customers (AcmeAI staging + FinVault production ring-1) with OTel tracing enabled.
Day 3-4: if stable, increase to 30% and then 100% for hosted; coordinate with Dedicated customer success teams for full rollout and schedule Private config bundles for customer ops.
Rollback: revert feature flag and redeploy previous runtime image; Dedicated customers can switch to pinned model variant while rollback completes.
Notes: Private customers receive tarball and install script with clear pre-upgrade checklist; require support window for on-prem upgrades.
SLA communication: draft status email to affected customers with ETA and mitigation steps (owner: Customer Success).
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Grafana panel longctx/ttft-compaction that surfaces compaction_count, compaction_duration_ms, kernel_fallback_count, worker_memory_headroom.
Add alert: TTFT 99p > baseline*2 for 10 minutes in longctx pools -> Pager to SRE and runtime-oncall.
Instrument trace spans 'kv_compact' and 'kernel_selector.decide' with sample rate 100% for canary pool.
Post-deploy: run smokejob (10m) every 30m for 48h to ensure TTFT < baseline*1.3.
